summary.text: John Tansey is a Democratic candidate for the Vermont House of Representatives, Windsor-1 District (two seats), in the November 3, 2026 general election, after finishing first in the August 11 Democratic primary ahead of incumbent John Bartholomew.

According to his campaign website, he is a Windsor native who has served as executive director of the Frank J. Guarini Institute for International Education at Dartmouth College for more than 20 years.

paragraphs.text: John Tansey says on his campaign website that he is a seventh-generation Vermonter, born and raised in Windsor.

After graduating from Windsor High School in 1980, he earned a bachelor's degree in applied economics and management from Cornell University, where he played football, and later a Master of Arts in Liberal Studies from Dartmouth College.

He worked in research administration at Dartmouth and spent seven years overseas with the Peace Corps, serving in the Philippines, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh and the Republic of Georgia, before taking the Guarini Institute post.

Tansey's site says he has been active in public service for nearly 40 years, serving on and chairing boards including the Windsor School Board, the Windsor Southeast Supervisory Union Board and the Windsor Selectboard, and the boards of trustees for Mount Ascutney Hospital and Valley Regional Hospital.
It adds that he served three years on the state Building Bright Futures Council after an appointment by Governor James Douglas.
He and his wife, Nida, have three children and six grandchildren, according to the site.
